page.layout: One page of text, single column; a small ornament and a catchword-style line "Yy 3 / Lega-" at the foot; no margin notes of substance on the right; a few faint marks at the left edge are the neighbouring page and are left out.

main_text.p: Vide Cic. lib. 5. Epist. ad Lucejum. Et Plutarch. in lib. Quâ quis ratione seipsum laudare queat.
Non placent, quem scurræ laudant, manipulares muffitant: Neq; illi, quorum linguaˇ gládiorum aciem præstringit domi : ut sunt Rhetores demagogi.

p.i: Malum istuc aliis videatur; quàm uti te collaudes.

main_text.head: LECTORUM.
main_text.p: Lectri sternebantur, sulciebantur, molliebantur, ut somno & amoribus essent aptiores.

page.notes: Printed words in the lower part were read with difficulty ("sulciebantur", "linguaˇ"); the ornament between the text and the foot is a printer's ornament and is not transcribed. The text "Lectorum" is a heading in spaced capitals. The initial "L" of "Lectri" is a large decorative letter joined to the first word; the reading "Lectri" is doubtful and may be "Lectisternebantur".
